p: silence before me: God as though he pleaded his cause with all nations requires silence, that he may be heard in his right.
renew their strength: That is, gather all their power and supports.

righteous man from the east: Who called Abraham (who was the pattern of God's justice in delivering his Church) from the idolatry of the Chaldeans to go to and fro at his commandment and placed him in the land of Canaan.
generations from the beginning: Who has created man and maintained his succession.
first: Though the world set up many gods, yet they diminish nothing of my glory: for I am all one, unchangeable, which have ever been and will be for ever.
feared: Considering my excellent works among my people.
came: They assembled themselves and conspired against me to maintain their idolatry.
Be of good courage: He notes the obstinacy of the idolaters to maintain their superstitions.
servant: And therefore ought not to pollute yourself with the superstition of the Gentiles.
right hand of my righteousness: That is, by the force of promise, in the performance of which I will show myself faithful and just.
find them: Because they will be destroyed.
worm Jacob: Thus he calls them because they were contemned of all the world, and that they considering their own poor estate should seek him for help.
mountains: I will make you able to destroy all your enemies no matter how mighty, and this chiefly is referred to the kingdom of Christ.
the poor and needy seek water: That is, they who will be afflicted in the captivity of Babylon.

land springs of water: God would rather change the order of nature than that they should want anything, who cry to him by true faith in their miseries: declaring to them by this that they will lack nothing by the way, when they return from Babylon.
hath created it: That is, has appointed and determined that it will come to pass.

Produce your cause: He bids the idolaters to prove their religion and to bring forth their idols, that they may be tried whether they know all things, and can do all things, which if they cannot do, he concludes that they are not gods, but vile idols.
chooseth you: So that a man cannot make an idol, without doing that which God detests and abhors for he chooses his own devises and forsakes the Lords.
and he shall come: Meaning, the Chaldeans.

call upon my name: That is, Cyrus, who will do all things in my name and by my direction: by which he means that both their captivity and deliverance will be ordered by God's providence and appointment.
princes as upon morter: Both of the Chaldeans and others.
your words: Meaning, that none of the Gentile gods can work any of these things.
them: That is, the Israelites who return from the captivity.
one that bringeth good tidings: That is, a continual succession of prophets and ministers.
I beheld: When I looked whether the idols could do these things, I found that they had neither wisdom nor power to do anything: therefore he concludes that all are wicked that trust in such vanities.
